solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A yard short? Just a shade

indicators.note: something short is missing a bit at its end, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
a quad (quadrangle) is a college yard or courtyard

explanation.surface: Someone a yard shy of a target shrugs that it's only a shade off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just a shade' reads as 'only slightly', but 'a shade' is the definition, a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is a pale greenish-blue colour, one particular tint among the blues.

clue.text: US director of play returning after three months

indicators.note: after places the word it governs behind the piece named next, so the returning piece comes second

parts.note: a quarter of the year is three months
coming back

explanation.surface: An American theatre director comes home after a three-month absence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director of play' suggests the theatre, but the play is a move in American football.
explanation.definitionFit: In American football the quarterback calls and runs the team's attacking plays on the field.

clue.text: Mock playing of messed up tragic aria, never finishing

indicators.note: words that never finish stop short, so each of the three words drops its final letter
something messed is jumbled, so the shortened letters are put into a new order

parts.note: up without its last letter
tragic without its last letter
aria without its last letter

explanation.surface: A sneering take on a botched operatic aria that never reaches its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messed up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' is fodder too, losing its P like the other two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Air guitar is miming playing a guitar with no instrument, a pretend or mock performance.

clue.text: Very upset of course one will be loud

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the following letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Of course someone very upset will raise their voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocal and noisy in a clamorous way; a vociferous protester is a loud one.

clue.text: Painter to alter course without sign of hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to veer is to change direction
the hesitant noise someone makes while thinking

explanation.surface: An artist told to change direction does so without hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of outside, so the hesitation goes inside the change of course.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was the Dutch Golden Age artist of Girl with a Pearl Earring.

clue.text: As soldier maybe apprehended and ordered for hearing?

definitions.text: As soldier maybe apprehended and ordered for hearing?
definitions.note: the whole clue describes a soldier tried by a military court

indicators.note: something for hearing is meant to be listened to, so the words are judged by how they sound

parts.note: apprehended means caught, which sounds like a law court
ordered means marshalled, which sounds like the military word martial

explanation.surface: A soldier is arrested and sent for a hearing, as in a military trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves sound like the answer: caught, then marshalled. The whole clue also describes the event, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier who is court-martialled is tried before a military tribunal, after arrest and an order to attend the hearing.

clue.text: Put up in full a redefined description of eg Australia's government

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means reading it from bottom to top, backwards
the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters running from the end of full to the start of redefined

explanation.surface: A redefined account of Australia's government is set out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a federation of states, so its government is described as federal.

clue.text: Waves round cane after beating

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: a beaten thing is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone waves a cane around after a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The waves' is a poetic name for the sea, so waves can stand for the ocean.

clue.text: Fight to begin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a noun, a scrap or brawl
second meaning: a verb phrase, to start work eagerly

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a call to start fighting; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a quarrel or brief scrap, and to set to is to start working on something.

clue.text: Area for rides maybe just turned to dust?

parts.note: fair means just or equitable
ground into powder

explanation.surface: A place for rides that has crumbled into dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just turned' reads as 'only recently turned', but just is a separate piece meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is the open site where roundabouts and other amusement rides are set up.

clue.text: Hide from army officer on exercises

parts.note: PE is physical education
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: Someone takes cover from an officer leading drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' is a noun, an animal's skin, not a verb; 'on' puts the officer after the exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelt is the skin of an animal with its fur, which is also called a hide.

clue.text: Old physician from this country heartlessly pinched clothes

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it, so the shortened word goes around the other piece
without its heart, the word loses its middle letter

parts.note: pinched means stole
the setter's country, the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A doctor of old heartlessly stole clothing in this country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as a noun, garments, but it is a verb: STLE clothes UK.
explanation.definitionFit: St Paul calls Luke the evangelist 'the beloved physician', so the saint is an ancient doctor.

clue.text: Become keen on following act

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so the keen-on piece is placed second, after the act

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act in a show
being into something means being keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone grows fond of the act that comes next on the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' places the keen-on piece after the act.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn into something is to change and become it, as a caterpillar becomes a butterfly.

clue.text: Publication of article on whacking children

parts.note: the definite article
whacking means huge, as in a whacking great bill
issue is a formal word for offspring

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about corporal punishment of children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whacking' suggests hitting children, but it is an adjective meaning very large. THE BIG ISSUE is a British street magazine sold by homeless vendors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Big Issue is a weekly magazine, a publication sold on the streets to help homeless people.

clue.text: Flaw ultimately slowing down legal document

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of flaw
rit. is the musical abbreviation for ritardando, slowing down

explanation.surface: A defect that ends up delaying a court paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written order issued by a court, a kind of legal document.

clue.text: Concrete parking area, note, daughter's given once more

parts.note: concrete means real, tangible
a parking lot is a car park
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A concrete car park note shows the daughter's space was handed over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concrete' looks like the material of the car park, but it is a separate piece meaning real.
explanation.definitionFit: To reallot is to distribute or assign again, so something reallotted has been handed out a second time.

clue.text: Revolutionary way to drink a little bit? Little passes their lips!

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
to sip is to drink a little
a part is a portion, a bit

explanation.surface: A radical method for drinking in small sips.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'little passes their lips' meaning both little food and few words.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappist monks follow a strict rule of silence and frugal diet, so hardly anything passes their lips.

clue.text: Invented wonderful new act? Dire!

parts.note: fab is slang for fabulous

indicators.note: a new version is a remade form, so the letters are set out afresh

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at a supposedly wonderful new act.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fabricated is made up or concocted, a synonym for invented.

clue.text: One supplying purchase of humble pie over the counter?

parts.note: eating crow, like eating humble pie, means admitting you were wrong
a bar is a counter where drinks are served

explanation.surface: A shop sells humble pie over the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying, but here it means grip or leverage; 'over' places CROW above BAR in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar is a lever, and leverage or grip on something is called purchase.

clue.text: Welfare service not keeping you in the dark?

definitions.text: Welfare service not keeping you in the dark?

parts.words: not keeping you in the dark
parts.note: surface reading: a service that is open and tells you everything

parts.words: Welfare service not keeping you in the dark
parts.note: setter's reading: looking after people only in daylight hours, not overnight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not keeping you in the dark' sounds like transparency, but it literally means care that ends before night falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Day care looks after children or vulnerable adults during the daytime, a welfare service that does not provide overnight stays.

clue.text: Run for charity to cross desert

indicators.note: one piece crosses the other by going inside it, so it is placed within

parts.note: aid is help, as given by a charity
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A charity run across the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' is an adjective here, as in a desert island.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert land is dry and barren, so desert used as an adjective means arid.

clue.text: Agree in short to put on Los Angeles, a musical

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: OK means agreed
LA is the usual abbreviation for Los Angeles
in means at home
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone briefly agrees to stage a musical in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agree in short' looks like a single abbreviation, but 'in' is its own piece, HOME cut short; LA is put on between OK and HOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical of 1943.

clue.text: Someone unique, exuding energy — not seen every day

indicators.note: exuding means giving off, so the named letter leaves the phrase

parts.note: a one-off is a unique person or thing
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A unique person, now low on energy, is rarely seen.
explanation.definitionFit: An on-off thing is intermittent, happening now and then rather than continuously.

clue.text: Watch that has fifty percent silver inside going slow

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the shortened word sits in the other

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or watch

indicators.note: fifty percent is half, so only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: argent is silver in heraldry

explanation.surface: A watch with half silver inside is running slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' reads as a timepiece, but it is the old interjection lo, look. ARGENT is the heraldic term for silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction for a very slow, broad tempo, so the music is going slow.

clue.text: City professional, indeed very good, apparently close to title

parts.note: yup is slang for yes, indeed
pi is slang for pious, seemingly very good

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of title

explanation.surface: A City worker who seems righteous is close to getting a title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The City' is London's financial district. 'Apparently' is fair because pi suggests sanctimonious, outwardly holy.
explanation.definitionFit: A yuppie is a young urban professional, the stereotype of the well-paid City worker of the 1980s.

clue.text: Giant act of self-harm concerning

parts.note: an own goal (OG) is scored against your own side
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A giant's self-harming act is worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concerning' looks like an adjective, worrying, but it is the preposition re.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogres are man-eating giants of folklore and fairy tales.

clue.text: Biblical tale Muslim's greeting, first to last, in a low voice

indicators.note: in places the rotated word within the other
the opening letter moves to the end, rotating the word

parts.note: the bass is the lowest male singing voice
salaam means peace, an Arabic greeting

explanation.surface: A Bible story features a Muslim greeting spoken in a low voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition can be read as 'Biblical tail', since the answer is a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers 22 tells how Balaam's donkey saw an angel and spoke to its master, a famous Bible story.

clue.text: Swapped tips on cool place for wellies that walker can use

indicators.note: the tips are the opening letters of two words, and swapping them exchanges those letters

parts.note: a fridge for keeping a boot cool, the boot being the wellies

explanation.surface: Instructions for swapping the toe caps on cold-storage wellingtons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellies' are wellington boots, rubber boots; their cool place is a BOOT FRIDGE, with B and F swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A footbridge is a bridge for pedestrians only, something a walker can use.

clue.text: Eject from seat on bus at terminal

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across answer, so the seat follows the bus piece
the terminal is the end, so only the word's final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of bus
a pew is a seat in a church

explanation.surface: Someone is thrown off their seat when the bus reaches the terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' reads as a bus station, but it means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to eject or spit out forcibly, especially vomit.
